articles.title: Taiz Residents Bury 18 Victims of Houthi Shelling
articles.description: TAIZ-SABA Residents of Taiz Governorate on Friday buried 18 victims, most of them civilians, including Mushira and her father, who were killed when Iranian-backed Houthi militias shelled their home on Mount Saber. Funeral prayers were held at Al-Saeed Mosque in Taiz City, attended by Governor Nabil Shamsan, local officials, military and security leaders, political party representatives, and large crowds of mourners. Governor Shamsan offered condolences to the victims’ families and wished the wounded a speedy recovery. He said the attacks would only strengthen Taiz residents’ determination to continue the national struggle to liberate the governorate and break the Houthi siege.

articles.title: The economy wounded by the war also marks Israel's elections
articles.description: The cost of rent, shopping, transport and bills has become one of the main concerns for Israeli families. Four days before the October 27th elections, many are wondering if the next government will be able to ease this pressure after more than three years of war and high military spending. Security remains central to the campaign, but the economy also weighs on the vote. A survey by the research center Israel Democracy Institute (IDI) indicates that the cost of living and the economy are priorities for 38% of Jewish respondents and 46% of Arabs. A malaise that is especially concentrated on the rising cost of housing and food, two structural problems that have been dragging on for years.
